items.title: Joe Lyde Interview, 1959-05-18
items.q: And then I played, Paggio had a big sore on his lip the size of a penny, this Mardi Gras. And I played for his trumpet for three or four hours.

ctx.x: So, what would you call that? A walk-in? You were just walking in there?

That's right. Well, I've played with the Eureka before. The first time I ever played with them was Mardi Gras last year, not this year. 58, I just played one number. Everybody was loaded, you know, and Sheik wanted to rest, you see. Oh, it was late in the day. And then I played a big parade across the river, which was one of those parades where you go from everybody, different houses and have lots of drinks and that. I think it was the Young Men Olympians, I forget which one. Every time I go over there now,…
I left before. You mean on Mardi Gras day with the Zulus?
